question: As a December 2020, who is the Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Radha Krishna Mathur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Radha Krishna Mathur** was appointed as the first Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory of Ladakh on October 31, 2019.
 
• He is a retired IAS officer of the Tripura cadre from the 1977 batch and has served in various capacities in the Government of India.
 
• Before his appointment as the Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, he served as the Chief Information Commissioner of India.
 
• His appointment marked the official bifurcation of the state of Jammu and Kashmir into two Union Territories: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Territory of Ladakh**

 
 
• Ladakh was officially declared a Union Territory on October 31, 2019, following the abrogation of Article 370 by the Government of India.
 
• Ladakh is divided into two districts: Leh and Kargil.
 
• The Union Territory is known for its unique culture, beautiful landscapes, and strategic importance given its location bordering China and Pakistan.
 
• The administration of Ladakh is directly under the control of the Central Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Article 370**
 
 
• Article 370 of the Indian Constitution granted special autonomous status to the state of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• On August 5, 2019, the President of India issued a constitutional order abrogating Article 370, thus revoking the special status of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• This move led to the reorganization of the state into two Union Territories: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.
 
• The abrogation of Article 370 has been a subject of significant political and public debate in India and internationally.
 
 
 
• **Chief Information Commissioner of India**
 
 
• The Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) is the head of the Central Information Commission, an apex body established under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
 
• The CIC is responsible for addressing complaints and appeals pertaining to the Right to Information (RTI) Act.
 
• The role of the CIC is crucial in ensuring transparency and accountability in the functioning of public authorities in India.
 
• The CIC has the authority to order disclosure of information and impose penalties on public authorities for non-compliance with the RTI Act.
